findings.title: Two-zone comfort penalty halves each zone's floor price; shipped plans sit up to 0.46 K below min_temp
findings.claim: On the stock two-zone house (tests/golden.py:make, winter_cold) the shipped plan's upper zone falls below min_temp 17.0 by 2.467 degree-steps summed over 12 price x DHW cells (1.314 in two|dhw|winter_typical, coldest 16.54 C), while the same house single-zone breaches 0.147 and every flat-price cell 0.
findings.mechanism: _comfort_terms (and _comfort_terms_batch) average the two zones' penalties with 0.5 x (...), which also halves each zone's quadratic floor term and its _COMFORT_FLOOR_L1 linear term; the constant's own comment says 2.0 is the smallest L1 that removes residual floor violations, so each zone of a two-zone house gets half of it and the solver buys the breach back where prices reward it (two|dhw|winter_typical: holding the floor costs 70.52 vs 67.50 SEK).

evidence.machine: L4 leads box: 4-vCPU Linux container, CPython 3.14 (venv314), OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: other leads seats shared the box; counts are contention-immune
evidence.tolerance: exact on one BLAS build; +-0.05 degree-steps across builds

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.optimizer:HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize (shipped upper/lower_temp_trajectory), via optimizer:HeatPumpOptimizer._comfort_terms / _comfort_terms_batch and the module constant _COMFORT_FLOOR_L1

perturbation.change: --perturb: optimizer._COMFORT_FLOOR_L1 2.0 -> 4.0 in memory (each zone gets the single-zone linear floor price)

findings.metric_definition: sum over steps and zones of max(0, min_temp - T_zone) of the shipped two-zone trajectories, over 6 price profiles x DHW on/off at winter_cold, 24 h
findings.phenomenon_property: Each zone of a two-zone plan pays the same price per degree-step below min_temp as a single-zone room does, so the floor the L1 term exists to pin holds per zone.

null_control.note: same house single-zone and the flat-price cells; the breach is price-bought and two-zone-specific

findings.proposed_fix_scope: optimizer.py _comfort_terms/_comfort_terms_batch: keep the two-zone average for the pull and the overshoot, but price each zone's undershoot (quadratic and L1) at the single-zone weight; pin with a two-zone winter_typical floor check.

findings.title: Setup overview page and setup diagram publish English slot text on a Swedish install
findings.claim: With the Swedish translation active, 22 of the 23 text lines the setup_overview flow page renders, all 16 slot labels describe_setup publishes (setup_topology, drawn verbatim by the card) and all 3 sensor_advisor labels are byte-identical to the English install's, while the narrative on the same plan sensors is Swedish (0 of 1 identical).
findings.mechanism: topology._SLOTS holds English literal labels and render_text_summary English headings; describe_setup, render_text_summary and rank_sensor_advisor take no language, so config_flow._setup_overview_form fills the sv template's {setup_summary} with English and the plan sensors publish English labels; narrative.render, by contrast, picks TEMPLATES[language].

evidence.unit: published strings identical en/sv (22 page lines + 16 slot labels + 3 advisor labels)
evidence.machine: L4 leads box: 4-vCPU Linux container, CPython 3.14 (venv314), OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: other leads seats shared the box; counts are contention-immune

findings.phenomenon_property: Every user-facing string the backend publishes for the setup diagram and the sensor advisor follows the instance language, as the narrative does.

null_control.note: narrative.render on the same sensors follows the language

findings.proposed_fix_scope: topology.py: slot labels and summary headings keyed by translation key (resolved from strings/translations by hass.config.language in the flow, or published as keys the card translates); config_flow/sensor call sites pass the language.

findings.title: sysid cannot adopt its own exact noise-free fit on 43 of 80 preset houses, yet arms on all 80
findings.claim: Driving the production step experiment on a plant exactly equal to the declared one with a noise-free reading, over every BuildingPreset structure x era x emitter at 3.5 and 6 kW, 19 of 80 cells complete and are refused by adoption_decision (heat-loss half-width 0.096-0.234 against the ln 1.10 = 0.0953 bar, fit error 0.0000) and 24 abort as 'fitted parameters outside plausible bounds'; all 80 arm.
findings.mechanism: The adoption bar keys on slab_ua_adoption_halfwidth, which at zero noise is set by the prior and window design, not by the fit's error, so light, radiator-heated and low-energy houses never reach it; separately the fit's plausibility box (tau 0.1-200 h, UA 0.01-5) rejects exact-data fits on masonry, low-energy and slab-floor cells (not separated here: true parameters outside the box versus a fit that misses them).

evidence.unit: cells of 80 refused at zero bias (plus 24 plausibility aborts)
evidence.machine: L4 leads box: 4-vCPU Linux container, CPython 3.14 (venv314), OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: other leads seats shared the box; counts are contention-immune

findings.metric_definition: preset cells whose exact-plant, noise-free sysid experiment completes and adoption_decision refuses (80 = 4 structures x 5 eras x 2 emitters x 2 pump sizes)
findings.phenomenon_property: A sysid experiment the tree arms on a declared plant can adopt its own exact answer: at zero bias and zero noise the gate admits and the plausibility box contains the fit.

null_control.note: the same drive admits exact fits on 37 cells (e.g. heavier pre-1980 houses), so the drive can admit

reproduction_steps: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub /home/claude/venv314/bin/python tools/audit/round9/D14/s3/p5_gate.py (D14-s3's light_new rows: hw 0.1446 at every zero-bias source)
findings.proposed_fix_scope: sysid.py: arm only where the declared plant's zero-noise half-width clears the bar and its parameters lie in the plausibility box (refuse at arm time with a reason), or size the window/step so they do; widen the box to the presets' own range.

findings.title: Grid-fee bounds are SEK numbers: a 0.05 EUR/kWh fee is unenterable in HUF, ISK, JPY and KRW
findings.claim: A 0.05 EUR/kWh transfer fee converted into each of 12 instance currencies draws 8 blocking verdicts across 4 currencies (HUF, ISK, JPY, KRW): the rules text is refused as implausible (HUF, KRW), the fixed-fee field's selector caps it at 5 in any currency (all four), and an entity-mode fee raises the grid_fee_magnitude repair (HUF, KRW); SEK, EUR, NOK and DKK draw 0.
findings.mechanism: grid_fee.IMPLAUSIBLE_FEE_SEK_PER_KWH = 10.0 (read by spec_problem and coordinator._audit_grid_fee) and the grid_fee_fixed NumberSelector max 5 are fixed numbers sized for SEK, while the same widget's unit and the repair text follow hass.config.currency.

evidence.unit: blocking verdicts (3 seams x 12 currencies); 4 currencies
evidence.machine: L4 leads box: 4-vCPU Linux container, CPython 3.14 (venv314), OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: other leads seats shared the box; counts are contention-immune
evidence.tolerance: exact given the stated exchange-rate table

perturbation.change: --perturb: IMPLAUSIBLE_FEE_SEK_PER_KWH 10 -> 1e6 in memory (grid_fee and the coordinator's imported copy)

findings.metric_definition: seam verdicts refusing or capping a 0.05 EUR/kWh fee expressed in each of 12 currencies at a stated rate table (rules refusal, fixed selector max, repair raised)
findings.phenomenon_property: Every magnitude bound on a money field scales with the instance currency the field is labelled in, so a fee that is ordinary in that currency is accepted without a repair.

null_control.note: the currencies the constants were sized for

findings.proposed_fix_scope: grid_fee.py/config_flow.py/coordinator.py: derive the implausibility bound and the fixed-fee selector max from the instance currency (a per-currency scale, or a bound relative to the published spot prices) rather than SEK constants.

findings.title: README's SEK currency fallback is unreachable under Home Assistant core, which defaults Config.currency to EUR
findings.claim: README.md says money is labelled 'SEK when the instance has none', but resolve_currency returns FALLBACK_CURRENCY for 0 of 2 Home Assistant core versions (2025.2.0, hacs.json's minimum, and 2026.2.3): core's Config.__init__ sets currency 'EUR', so an instance that never chose a currency is labelled EUR; only the test stub (FakeHass, currency 'SEK') produces SEK.
findings.mechanism: currency.resolve_currency falls back only on a falsy hass.config.currency; HA core initialises it to 'EUR' and validates a configured value, so the fallback and the README/docstring rationale describe the test double, not the counterpart.

evidence.unit: HA core versions (of 2) reaching the SEK fallback
evidence.machine: L4 leads box: 4-vCPU Linux container, CPython 3.14 (venv314), OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: reads HA core wheels fetched with pip download --no-deps into a mktemp root (or --wheels DIR)

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.currency:resolve_currency, fed HA core homeassistant/core_config.py:Config.__init__'s currency default (AST-read from the wheel)

perturbation.change: --perturb: currency.resolve_currency replaced in memory by lambda hass: FALLBACK_CURRENCY

findings.metric_definition: HA core versions for which resolve_currency on core's own Config.currency default returns FALLBACK_CURRENCY
findings.phenomenon_property: What the README and currency.py say an unconfigured instance shows is what Home Assistant core delivers, not what the test stub pins.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: README.md line 450 and currency.py's docstring: state that the label is hass.config.currency (EUR on an instance that never set one); keep or drop the dead fallback deliberately.
